# Run security awareness training

[Overview](#overview) · [Before you start](#before-you-start) · [Steps](#steps-at-a-glance)

## Overview

When onboarding people or refreshing the organization's security practices. Role-appropriate training completed by the assigned people with follow-up for observed gaps.

Start with the applicability facts and evidence listed in the first step. Resolve missing facts before authorizing the affected work. Completion requires the documented outcome, including tracked exceptions; starting an application or recording a task is not evidence of completion.

> This is an operational coordination guide. Confirm the applicable company facts, contracts and jurisdictions before acting. The cited authorities describe their named jurisdictions or frameworks; their rules are not asserted for other countries. External actions require approval for the specific action.

## Step details

<a id="step-1"></a>

### 1. Identify relevant roles and security behaviors

agent-runnable


Map workers and contractors to the systems, data and threats they encounter. Include reporting, credential protection, payment fraud and remote work, and distinguish required training from optional material.

- Sources: [FTC cybersecurity for small business](https://www.ftc.gov/business-guidance/small-businesses/cybersecurity)

<a id="step-2"></a>

### 2. Approve the training and exercise approach

human · human approval required


Security and HR owners select accessible materials and realistic scenarios. Review privacy and employment implications of simulations and avoid collecting credentials or humiliating participants.

- Sources: [FTC cybersecurity for small business](https://www.ftc.gov/business-guidance/small-businesses/cybersecurity)

<a id="step-3"></a>

### 3. Deliver training and safe practice

human · human approval required


The assigned people complete their own training and practice the reporting process. Provide a supported route for questions and accommodations and record participation without treating an agent-generated answer as employee completion.

- Sources: [FTC cybersecurity for small business](https://www.ftc.gov/business-guidance/small-businesses/cybersecurity)

<a id="step-4"></a>

### 4. Assess understanding and operational follow-through

agent-runnable


Review permitted assessment results, reported concerns and recurring errors. Check that staff can find contacts and use the security process rather than relying only on an attendance count.

- Sources: [FTC cybersecurity for small business](https://www.ftc.gov/business-guidance/small-businesses/cybersecurity)

<a id="step-5"></a>

### 5. Assign targeted follow-up and refresh content

human · human approval required


Owners address gaps with appropriate coaching and control changes. Update the material after incidents, system changes or emerging threats and retain the completion evidence under the approved policy.

- Verify: Role-appropriate training completed by the assigned people with follow-up for observed gaps.
- Sources: [FTC cybersecurity for small business](https://www.ftc.gov/business-guidance/small-businesses/cybersecurity)
